messages.content:
You are a craft auditor measuring ARCHETYPE MANIFESTATION COLLAPSE in a romance scene. An archetype is a MOVEMENT (a way of responding under pressure), not a line. The failure we are hunting: the writer keeps expressing the archetype the SAME way every story instead of selecting the reaction that fits THIS situation.

You will be given the love interest's archetype, its canonical (heterogeneous) manifestation menu, a normalized reaction-category repertoire, and the scene. The love interest may be ONSTAGE or only RECALLED/remembered (in an opening scene he is often offstage — classify remembered behavior too). Identify:
  1. The STIMULUS — what in the scene the love interest is reacting to (e.g. "she pressed him for the truth", "she cried", "she flirted", "she accused him", "she asked for help", or "nothing — he initiated"). If he is only recalled, the stimulus is whatever the memory is about.
  2. The DOMINANT reaction category (one), and any other present categories, from the repertoire.
  3. The specific GESTURE — the actual on-page/recalled behavior in ≤15 words.
  4. Whether that gesture is one of the archetype's canonical MENU forms or a fresh manifestation.

If the love interest exhibits NO behavior at all (not onstage, not recalled, not referenced), return dominant_category "ABSENT". Be honest and specific — do not invent behavior that is not in the text. Return strict JSON, no prose.

LOVE INTEREST: Julian
ARCHETYPE: SPELLBINDER (Spellbinder)
MOVEMENT: PULLS FEELING INTO HIS GRAVITY — he does not chase, does not announce, does not perform. The room reorganizes toward him whether he wants it to or not. Stillness is his velocity.
CANONICAL MANIFESTATION MENU (heterogeneous on purpose — verbal/behavioral/spatial/cognitive/affective):
    • (spatial) the room reorganizes around him; conversations bend toward where he stands without him moving
    • (affective) a silence he can pull from a room without speaking
    • (behavioral) letting other people come to him; he does not cross floors
    • (verbal) a single sentence that ends an argument three other people were trying to win
    • (affective) a stillness so real other men have to perform stillness to be near it
    • (cognitive) refusing to perform what the room is performing — the only person not flattering the senior partner

NORMALIZED REACTION REPERTOIRE (classify INTO these):
    • humor_teasing — meets the moment with wit / a joke / teasing
    • subject_change — verbal redirect — changes the subject, answers a different question
    • practical_competence — fixes / solves / handles the problem instead of addressing the feeling
    • protective_action — steps in front of / shields / absorbs a cost for her
    • indirect_care — a small unacknowledged kindness; help he refuses to take credit for
    • withdrawal — goes quiet / closed / opaque but stays in the room
    • premature_exit — leaves — physically exits before the moment can land
    • direct_vulnerability — drops the armor — says the real thing, lets feeling show undressed
    • challenge_provocation — pushes back / tests her / provokes rather than soothes
    • stillness_presence — lets it land — does not deflect, holds the moment, stays present in silence

SCENE PROSE:
TEMPTATION ||| Let the blade slip from my fingers onto the ground. ||| “Let’s see what happens if I don’t answer.”  
BOUNDARY ||| Step back, pulling my hand away from his. ||| “I won’t play your game in front of them.”  
CONFESSION ||| Hold his gaze, fingers trembling around the blade. ||| “I feel trapped between what I want and what you demand.”  
REVERSAL ||| Take a step forward, reclaiming the blade. ||| “I’ll decide how this unfolds — your questions, my answers.”  
SILENCE ||| Stand still, breath shaky, staring at the question in my hand. |||

Return ONLY this JSON:
{
  "stimulus": "<what he is reacting to, ≤12 words — or \"none — he initiated\">",
  "dominant_category": "<one repertoire key | ABSENT>",
  "present_categories": [<repertoire keys actually shown>],
  "gesture": "<the specific behavior, ≤15 words, quote if possible>",
  "in_menu": <true|false>,
  "reason": "<one sentence: why this category, and whether the reaction is selected by the situation or is a default tic>"
}
